lines.text: One wrong number… and the whole AI training crashes.
AI learns by walking downhill. High means very wrong. Low, less wrong. The bottom is the right answer.
Each step, it checks the slope and multiplies it by one number: the learning rate. It sets how big each step is.
Too small? It inches along… and barely gets anywhere.
Just right? It lands right on target.
Too big? It bounces wall to wall… and flies right out.
Same problem. Only one number changed.
That's why big models like GPT-3 don't use one fixed number. They warm up, peak, then slow down.
Comment a learning rate, and I'll run yours in the next reel.

notes: hold = minimum seconds from this line's start to the next line's start (the beat length). Lines that run long stretch their beat. kokoro_voice/kokoro_speed are for the offline voice (scripts/gen/kokoro_tts.py); speed is for HeyGen.
